s1.syndrome_frame: Painless testicular swelling with associated epididymal involvement and adrenal gland abnormalities
salient_findings: Enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis
key_facts: 82-year-old man
Painless right testicular swelling of several weeks’ duration
No systemic symptoms
History of glaucoma, prostatic adenomectomy, and hernioplasty
Medications: dorzolamide, lansoprazole, and dutasteride
Testicular ultrasound showed enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis
Ipsilateral hydrocele
Swelling persisted after 10 days of amoxicillin–clavulanate
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT confirmed testicular pathology
New bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement
Adrenal nodules were absent on a CT scan 3 years earlier
18 FDG PET/CT showed intense uptake in the right testis
No uptake in the adrenal glands
Normal laboratory evaluation
Negative serologies for active HCV and EBV
Positive for past EBV

shortlist.label: Leydig cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Painless testicular swelling and intense uptake on 18 FDG PET/CT

shortlist.label: Testicular lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Testicular swelling and epididymal involvement, with potential for adrenal involvement

shortlist.label: Seminoma
shortlist.why_kept: Painless testicular swelling and potential for metastasis to adrenal glands

shortlist.label: Adrenal metastasis from testicular cancer
shortlist.why_kept: New bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement and history of testicular pathology

shortlist.label: Testicular cancer with adrenal metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: Testicular swelling, epididymal involvement, and new adrenal gland abnormalities

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of painless testicular swelling and the ultrasound findings of testicular enlargement and inhomogeneity, along with the intense uptake on the 18 FDG PET/CT, are consistent with a testicular tumor. The lack of systemic symptoms and normal laboratory evaluation also support this diagnosis. Leydig cell tumors are known to be a type of testicular cancer that can present with painless testicular swelling and can have variable metabolic activity on PET/CT.

rejected.label: Testicular lymphoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with systemic symptoms and abnormal laboratory findings, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Seminoma
rejected.why: Usually presents with testicular swelling and may have elevated LDH or β2-microglobulin, which are not elevated in this case

rejected.label: Adrenal metastasis from testicular cancer
rejected.why: The adrenal nodules showed no uptake on the 18 FDG PET/CT, making metastasis less likely

rejected.label: Testicular cancer with adrenal metastasis
rejected.why: Similar to the previous reason, the lack of uptake in the adrenal glands on the 18 FDG PET/CT makes this diagnosis less likely
